title: HVAC controls and hidden vent usability
summary: Reviews in this topic mainly describe hard-to-find climate controls, hidden or poorly aimed vents, and inconvenient touchscreen-based adjustment of heating and cooling.

positive.summary: One positive review praises the instrument interface rather than the heating or cooling controls themselves, so positive evidence for this topic is limited.

negative.summary: Negative reviews focus on confusing or poorly located climate controls, hidden or hard-to-adjust vents, weak airflow direction, and frustration with needing the display instead of physical buttons or knobs.

undetermined.summary: Undetermined reviews mention delayed or poorly thought out heating and cooling operation, but the examples are too limited to classify a concrete sentiment pattern more precisely.

signal_notes.interpretation: ICE examples in this topic are associated with especially concentrated negative or mixed feedback about HVAC control location and vent usability compared with the rest of the engine-type breakdown, based on the supplied exploratory signal.

BEVE examples also show predominantly negative or mixed feedback on these HVAC controls and vents, with a pattern that appears similar to the rest of the engine-type breakdown in the supplied exploratory signal.

limitations: The sampled fragments are stratified and not representative of all owners or all G60 HVAC experiences.
The positive sample does not clearly address the HVAC control issue, so evidence for favorable views on this specific topic is minimal.
This cluster combines control placement, vent adjustability, airflow direction, and system response, so it spans several related but distinct usability concerns.
